headline: Personalised mRNA vaccine stops high-risk melanoma returning in a phase-three trial
youtube_title: Personalised mRNA vaccine stops high-risk melanoma returning in a phase-three trial

words.def_en: A medical treatment that helps the body prepare to fight a disease.
words.example_en: A new personalised vaccine given with a cancer drug has stopped skin cancer returning in patients during a major trial.

words.def_en: A serious type of skin cancer.
words.example_en: The vaccine was developed by Merck and Moderna and was given to people with high-risk melanoma after surgery.

words.def_en: A scientific test of a new treatment in a group of people.
words.example_en: A new personalised vaccine given with a cancer drug has stopped skin cancer returning in patients during a major trial.

words.def_en: Made for one specific person rather than for everyone.
words.example_en: A new personalised vaccine given with a cancer drug has stopped skin cancer returning in patients during a major trial.

words.def_en: A medical operation that cuts into the body to treat a problem.
words.example_en: The vaccine was developed by Merck and Moderna and was given to people with high-risk melanoma after surgery.

words.def_en: A cancer treatment that uses the body immune system.
words.example_en: The vaccine, called Intismeran, was given in combination with Keytruda, an immunotherapy drug already used in cancer treatment.

words.def_en: A lump of abnormal cells that can be cancer.
words.example_en: Merck and Moderna call this a personalised vaccine because it is built from an individual patient's tumour.

words.def_en: Able to resist or fight a disease.
words.example_en: It instructs the immune system to recognise and attack any tumour cells that remain after surgery.

words.def_en: A change in the DNA of a cell.

words.def_en: Two or more things used together.
